formulations.text: A real-valued discrete-time process (X_n)_{n≥0}, adapted to a filtration (F_n)_{n≥0} and satisfying E|X_n|<∞ for every n, is a martingale if E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n almost surely for each n≥0.

formulations.text: An integrable adapted real-valued discrete-time process (X_n,F_n)_{n≥0} is a martingale if E[X_m|F_n]=X_n almost surely whenever 0≤n≤m are integers.

context: Finite simple undirected graph with nonempty vertex set: least proper vertex coloring palette size
editorial_screening_reason: ProofWiki's direct Definition:Chromatic Number states the minimum positive integer k admitting a proper vertex k-coloring. The independently authored formulation specifies finite, loopless, nonempty simple undirected graphs to avoid distinct empty graph and loop conventions and clarifies palette semantics: a coloring may use fewer than k labels. It does not concern edge chromatic number or total chromatic number. MathWorld separately supports the positive chromatic polynomial alternative, but it remains held until a distinct source-registration/rights review permits that observation.

formulations.text: For a finite simple undirected graph G having at least one vertex, the chromatic number χ(G) is the smallest positive integer k for which there exists c:V(G)→{1,…,k} with c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}∈E(G).
